title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Paper Bills and Statements) Bill 2017
short_title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Paper Bills and Statements) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would make paper the default form for consumer bills and transaction records, allowing electronic delivery only when the customer agrees to it.
It would prohibit charges for transaction records and other bills, and require other bills supplied to consumers to be clear, legible and in plain language.
The rules would apply to goods and services supplied from commencement, which would occur on the day after the bill received Royal Assent.
changes: Proof of purchase would follow the paper default for transactions of $75 or more, and on request for smaller purchases.
Itemised bills would require customer consent before electronic delivery.
The delivery rules would override inconsistent provisions of the Electronic Transactions Act 1999.
Pecuniary penalty provisions would be updated to enforce the new obligations.
summary.affected: Suppliers of goods and services and consumers receiving bills, itemised accounts or transaction records are affected.
